response.rationale: All options are unmatched. Option D (Trousseau's syndrome) is most clinically relevant to the vignette's findings of elevated tumor markers and hypercoagulability. Option C (Thromboembolic stroke from hypercoagulable state) is a general description that fits the clinical picture. Option B (Cardioembolic stroke with underlying hypercoagulable state due to metastatic breast cancer and autoimmune hemolytic anemia) is more specific but less directly supported than D. Option A (Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis) is a less likely cause given the echocardiogram findings.
